recipes.name: Chicken and Chorizo Pasta Bake
ingredients_raw: 4 boneless chicken breasts, cut into 1/2 inch cubes

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain and set aside.

Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken, and cook until firm and lightly browned, about 5 minutes. Stir in the bell pepper and chorizo and cook for 5 minutes until the chorizo is hot and the chicken is no longer pink in the center. Remove from heat.

Pour the tomato puree, cream, and red pepper flakes into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer 5 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Add drained pasta and sauce to the skillet containing the chicken and mix well. Spoon the mixture into an oven proof dish. Sprinkle the Cheddar, mozzarella, and Parmesan cheese over the top. Bake 30 minutes, or until the top is golden and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Chorizo Pasta Bake
raw_recipe.description: Boneless chicken breasts, Spanish chorizo links, and penne is baked in a creamy tomato sauce topped with three cheeses.

review.reviewBody: A tasty recipe that makes great leftovers. I used milk instead of the heavy cream to lighten it up a bit. Nice flavor and easy to make.

Really yummy! Added extra mozzarella and extra Parmesan (doubled both) and mixed those plus the cheddar into the dish before baking, putting extra Parmesan for the top. Only used two chicken breasts and increased Chorizo to 1-1/2 # ground Chorizo (Spanish style, not Mexican). Was careful not to overcook the chicken (used 1 inch chunks instead of 1/2 inch). Added smoked paprika to the Chorizo while cooking. And added smoked paprika to entire dish at the end. Added salt and pepper to chicken while cooking. Included 1 chopped medium onion along with the chopped red pepper. Used 1/2 cup heavy cream and half cup of whole milk. Added a 14oz can of roasted diced tomatoes to the puree. Thickened the sauce with a tablespoon of flour and water. Included the optional 1/2 t. pepper flakes. Froze half of the mixture for another time. Definitely will make again.

I MADE THE FOLLOWING CHANGES., that's why I give it 5 stars

I used Rotel tomatoes w/chillies
half and half (guessed)
1/2 cup of Green Salsa
1/2 cup of cream cheese
Chopped Onions


I cooked the Chorizo first, and then cooked the chicken in the Chorizo juice, adding Sazon Goya seasoning (can be found in any aisle where there's hispanic food).

FYI: Chorizo has an interesting taste if you have never eaten it. I cooked mine up the night before making this recipe. I actually made it, and then wasn't sure what to do with it. Yay for All Recipes! 
This was great! I changed it up just a little bit: I used milk instead of the cream, red AND green pepper, shrimp instead of chicken, and one 6oz can of tomato paste mixed with 1/2 cup water, then added just a little spaghetti sauce with the milk and the red pepper flakes. YUM! We will definitely have this again. I loved it with shrimp and will throw in more next time. Husband liked it too.

I loved this, I used soy cherizo and chicken thighs. Used diced tomatoes that I ran through the food processor with red pepper flakes, pepper, garlic and onion powder. I also added onion and celery to the red pepper, cooked that all seperate from the meat. YUMMY! I used the onion and garlic powder and salt and pepper to the chicken before I cooked it. I had made sweet potato gniccoi last month so I boiled them then fried them and used that rather then penne. Loved this.

It was a tasty meal, I might make it again, but would probably tweak it more. Definitely was not a spicy dish (and I added a lot more red pepper flakes). I also seasoned it was Spanish Paprika and Cilantro. I used shrimp instead of chicken. I added an entire onion, an additional green bell pepper, used heavy cream because that's what I had on hand, and mixed in cheese before layering the top with the cheese.

Delicious! I was looking for something to do with chorizo and found this. I added some onion as well and used diced tomatoes and not tomato purée. Also used cheddar and Pepper Jack Cheeses as I had those on hand. I also had mini shell pasta and it was perfect.

I altered the recipe a bit. I added onion and garlic, used tinned tomatoes and tomato paste, with a good helping of Italian herb mix. I also used pizza cheese mix. My fussy adult daughter couldn’t get enough of it. I will definitely be making this again.

Very tasty and easy to make. I upped the recipe to 6 people so I could freeze some for another meal. 
I added half a sweet onion and three cloves of garlic and used two chorizo sausages, boneless chicken thighs and 3% milk. Thumps up!

Didn't have any peppers so I used onions. I also used 1lb ground chorizo, and prego chunky garden sauce, the whole jar, just for ease. It was delicious. My kids ate it all and my husband went back for seconds.

I did change a few things as we are trying to eat healthier I substituted wheat penne and added sun dried tomatoes and some basil apart from that the same oh and a little garlic easy to make left overs for the week a winner !
I made this with my dad (the famous Simon Wraight) He made it for my mum so she married him and here I am!
This was good but did need a little "spicing" up as it was sort of bland on its own. I also used less pasta but the same amount of sauce and am glad I did. It would have been very dry otherwise.
Amazingly creamy and flavourful
Used milk instead of cream and added sautéed onion and garlic to chicken . Was so good husband and I both had 2nd helpings!
I thought it was dry. I won't make again.
A terrific recipe, definitely a family favorite. Made it with leftover grilled chicken once, still worked out great
An easy bake, although without chilli flakes a little bland. Will definitely make it again but with extra flavourings.

Very easy to make! A favorite in my household as my fiancé is Puerto Rican, he loves the chorizo. I normally can’t eat it normally like, with eggs, but the chorizo in this casserole is subtle and not overpowering. I think the first time I made this, I only used half a tube of the chorizo. And always buy authentic. It makes a difference.
My wife compared it to lasagna and enchiladas, so of course this goes in our favorites file. We used tomato sauce rather than puree, heavy rather than light cream, and held out the red pepper flakes.
